summary: Go WebSearch has the public tool name, query/domain parameters, deferred-discovery metadata, stricter domain-list guards, and partial helper-level work for citation formatting, normalized result blocks, policy objects, and an injectable server-tool provider. It is not yet runtime-equivalent to the TS reference. The TS tool is a provider-native Anthropic web_search_20250305 server-tool flow inside a single model API call, with provider/model enablement, passthrough permission suggestions, streaming server_tool_use/web_search_tool_result progress, usage accounting, and a query/results/duration output object. The Go tool still defaults to a local DuckDuckGo-style pipeline, registers unconditionally, uses a stateful local cache, cannot express or parse the Anthropic server-tool protocol in the common provider/types layer, emits different progress and error lifecycles, and returns a different model-facing result shape.

gaps.title: Go production execution defaults to local DDG search instead of the TS Anthropic web_search server tool
gaps.description: TS constructs an Anthropic-defined web_search_20250305 tool schema, injects it through extraToolSchemas, and asks the model/API to perform search inside the streaming API call. Go has a WebSearchServerToolProvider scaffold, but NewWebSearchTool defaults to local_fallback, registry_setup.go only registers that default instance, and no production code wires SetWebSearchServerToolProvider. The common provider Params/ToolDefinition surface only supports ordinary client tools, so it cannot currently send the TS extra server-tool schema without a provider/type extension.

ts_evidence.note: makeToolSchema returns the Anthropic-defined tool {type:'web_search_20250305', name:'web_search', allowed_domains, blocked_domains, max_uses:8}.
call uses queryModelWithStreaming with system prompt, abort signal, model options, extraToolSchemas:[toolSchema], and querySource:'web_search_tool'.
The local TS contract harness marks WebSearch semantics as providerNative with progress events and resultShape query/results/durationSeconds.

go_evidence.note: WebSearchTool is documented and structured around local DuckDuckGo search plus optional providerSearch/serverTool fields.
NewWebSearchTool sets instant/lite DDG URLs and mode:webExecutionModeLocalFallback.
SetupRegistry creates NewWebSearchTool(webSearchCache), applies only static domain slices, and registers it without a provider-native server tool.
Provider Params has only ordinary Tools []types.ToolDefinition and ToolChoice; no extra server-tool schema channel.
ToolDefinition contains name/description/input_schema only, which cannot represent an Anthropic-defined {type:'web_search_20250305'} tool.
The existing gap test intentionally proves Go local_fallback normalized method differs from the TS provider_native harness.

gaps.impact: Core runtime parity gap: search quality, ranking, region/provider behavior, cancellation model, citations, usage accounting, and API semantics all diverge because Go is not using the same server-side search path.

gaps.title: Go provider/types cannot round-trip server_tool_use, web_search_tool_result, or web search usage
gaps.description: TS relies on Anthropic streaming content blocks server_tool_use and web_search_tool_result, including input_json_delta parsing and server_tool_use.web_search_requests usage. Go's Anthropic stream converter recognizes only text/tool_use/thinking blocks and Usage only contains token/cache fields. Unknown blocks can be preserved when deserializing stored messages, but the live Anthropic stream path drops unknown server-side block variants rather than preserving raw JSON or converting them into first-class WebSearch events.

ts_evidence.note: makeOutputFromSearchResponse expects server_tool_use and web_search_tool_result blocks and converts web_search_tool_result content into result objects.
The streaming loop tracks server_tool_use IDs, input_json_delta query JSON, and web_search_tool_result arrivals for progress.
TS accumulates usage.server_tool_use.web_search_requests into modelUsage.webSearchRequests.
TS normalizes message usage with server_tool_use.web_search_requests and web_fetch_requests.

go_evidence.note: ContentDelta has fields for text, thinking, tool_use id/name, and tool input partial_json only.
Usage lacks a server_tool_use/web_search_requests field.
ContentBlockStartEvent switch handles TextBlock, ToolUseBlock, and ThinkingBlock; no server_tool_use or web_search_tool_result case.
ContentBlockDeltaEvent switch handles text_delta, input_json_delta, and thinking_delta only.
Non-streaming fallback skips any Anthropic block not understood by anthropicBlockToEvents.
anthropicUsageToTypes copies token/cache counts only.

gaps.impact: Even if a server tool schema were sent, Go cannot faithfully observe, persist, display, or bill the server-side search lifecycle that TS depends on.

gaps.title: Go adds a local WebSearch result cache that TS does not have and cached hits change output semantics
gaps.description: TS WebSearch does not have a tool-local result cache; each call builds a server-tool schema and invokes queryModelWithStreaming. Go uses a 15-minute searchCache keyed by query and domain filters. On cache hit it manufactures a single result with title 'Cached result', URL 'cache://websearch', and snippet containing the previous formatted output, then emits that as if it were a real search result. This changes freshness, citations, source URLs, result counts, and progress behavior.

ts_evidence.note: The call path always creates a user message/tool schema and starts queryModelWithStreaming; no local cache is checked.
The final result is built from the current API stream content blocks and measured duration.

go_evidence.note: A reusable searchCache stores string results for 15 minutes with max entry eviction.
SetupRegistry creates a dedicated webSearchCache and injects it into NewWebSearchTool.
makeWebSearchCacheKey keys searches by normalized query plus allowed/blocked domains.
Cache hits return a synthetic searchResult with URL cache://websearch and emit a received-results event.
Local fallback stores the formatted output string and then returns a citation-formatted ToolResult.

gaps.impact: A repeated Go search can cite cache://websearch instead of the original sources and can return stale data where TS would make a fresh server-side request.

gaps.title: Go's model-facing and internal output shape does not match TS query/results/durationSeconds semantics
gaps.description: TS call returns an Output object with query, results array, and durationSeconds. Search result objects include tool_use_id and content entries with title/url only; mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam converts that into a text block with Links JSON and the sources reminder. Go directly returns types.ToolResult.Content plus ContentBlocks and Metadata, has no durationSeconds or search-count result object, lacks tool_use_id on WebSearchToolResultBlock, includes snippets in Links JSON, and returns plain 'No results found.' without the TS header/reminder path.

ts_evidence.note: TS output schema is {query, results: array<SearchResult|string>, durationSeconds}; SearchResult content entries are title/url only.
web_search_tool_result success maps to {tool_use_id, content:[{title,url}]} and final Output includes durationSeconds.
mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam renders header, string summaries, Links JSON or No links found, then the sources reminder.
TS result UI derives 'Did N searches in X' from output.results and output.durationSeconds.

go_evidence.note: Go tool outputs are generic ToolResult strings/content blocks/metadata, not the WebSearch-specific Output object.
WebSearchToolResultBlock has Type and Content only; WebSearchResultBlock includes snippet/cited_text/page_age but no tool_use_id wrapper.
FormatWebSearchToolResult serializes title/url plus optional snippet into Links JSON.
buildWebSearchStructuredResult emits progress TextBlocks, a websearch_result_json TextBlock, a WebSearchToolResultBlock, and metadata; no durationSeconds.
Empty local results return plain 'No results found.' with no Links JSON or sources reminder.

gaps.impact: Renderers, transcript compaction, search-result summarization, and model-facing citations can observe different structures and content than TS.

gaps.title: Server-tool errors are surfaced as TS result strings but Go falls through to local search
gaps.description: TS treats a web_search_tool_result whose content is an error object as a successful tool call containing the string 'Web search error: <error_code>' in results. Go runWebSearchServerTool converts ErrorCode into an error, and Execute ignores non-unavailable server-tool errors before continuing to providerSearch/local fallback. That can mask upstream web_search failures, return unrelated local DDG results, and lose the TS error string.

ts_evidence.note: If web_search_tool_result.content is not an array, TS logs and pushes 'Web search error: <error_code>' into results.
String result entries are rendered directly into the tool_result content.

go_evidence.note: runWebSearchServerTool turns resp.ErrorCode into fmt.Errorf('web_search server tool error: %s').
Go has helper types to detect and format web_search_tool_result_error, but Execute does not use them for server provider errors.
Execute tries serverTool only in provider_native mode; on any non-unavailable error it discards the error and falls through.
Tests assert provider errors are wrapped by runWebSearchServerTool, not rendered into a TS-style result string by Execute.

gaps.impact: Go can hide real server-tool failures behind fallback results and will not present the TS-visible error contract to the model.

gaps.title: Go progress events are not emitted at the same lifecycle points or with the same data as TS
gaps.description: TS progress is derived from streamed server_tool_use input_json_delta and web_search_tool_result block starts. It emits query_update only when the server tool query is known/changed and search_results_received with resultCount and the actual query. Go emits started/query_update before full validation and before policy checks, omits the query from search_results_received, emits fake received-results events for cache hits, and the provider-native serverTool branch currently returns without emitting search_results_received at all.

ts_evidence.note: TS accumulates input_json_delta, extracts the actual query, and emits query_update with toolUseID only when it changes.
TS emits search_results_received with resultCount and query when a web_search_tool_result block starts.
The progress renderer expects query_update.query and search_results_received.resultCount/query.

go_evidence.note: Go WebSearchProgressEvent has Type, Query, and Count but no resultCount field name or toolUseID.
Execute emits started and query_update before the allowed/blocked conflict validation returns.
Cache hits emit search_results_received for a synthetic cached result.
The serverTool success branch returns after building the result without emitting search_results_received.
The local fallback success branch emits search_results_received with Count only, not the query.

gaps.impact: TUI/status clients and transcript consumers will show different or misleading search progress, especially for invalid inputs, cached hits, and provider-native calls.

gaps.title: Go lacks TS provider/model enablement and WebSearch-specific permission suggestion behavior
gaps.description: TS WebSearch is only exposed when the active API provider/model supports it and checkPermissions returns a passthrough decision with a localSettings allow-rule suggestion. tools.ts also filters denied tools before applying isEnabled. Go registers WebSearch unconditionally in SetupRegistry, has no per-tool isEnabled method in the Tool interface, and relies on a generic permission handler that only receives ToolName/Input without WebSearch-specific passthrough message or localSettings suggestion data.

ts_evidence.note: isEnabled allows firstParty, Foundry, and Vertex Claude 4 model families, and disables all other providers/models.
checkPermissions returns behavior:'passthrough', message:'WebSearchTool requires permission.', and an addRules suggestion for localSettings.
filterToolsByDenyRules strips blanket-denied tools before they are visible to the model.
getTools filters allowed tools by each tool's isEnabled() result.

go_evidence.note: The Go Tool interface has Name, Description, Schema, and Execute only; no isEnabled or checkPermissions hook.
SetupRegistry always registers WebSearch after optional domain slice assignment.
PermissionRequest carries SessionID, ToolName, Input, Mode, and AvoidPrompts only; it has no suggestion payload equivalent.
Permission denial becomes a generic 'Permission denied for tool' result; there is no WebSearch passthrough suggestion lifecycle.
WebSearch has deferred discovery metadata, but that is discovery visibility only and not provider/model enablement.

gaps.impact: Go can advertise WebSearch for providers/models where TS would hide it, and cannot reproduce the TS approval UX or localSettings rule suggestion semantics.

gaps.title: WebSearch request usage is not tracked in Go session usage or cost state
gaps.description: TS carries server_tool_use.web_search_requests through API usage normalization, modelUsage, cost tracking, stats, and session summaries. Go's Usage type and session accumulation only account for tokens/cache fields. Because the local fallback is not an Anthropic server tool and the provider layer cannot parse server_tool_use usage, Go cannot display or cost web search request counts like TS.

ts_evidence.note: TS usage initializes server_tool_use with web_search_requests and web_fetch_requests.
TS aggregates totalUsage.server_tool_use.web_search_requests across messages.
TS includes webSearchRequests in tracked deltas and user-visible usage summaries.
TS cost calculation prices usage.server_tool_use.web_search_requests.

go_evidence.note: Go Usage has input/output/cache token fields only.
MessageDelta usage conversion records output tokens only.
anthropicUsageToTypes records token/cache counts only.
Session usage accumulation adds token/cache counts only.
Go cost tracking builds cost.TokenUsage from token/cache fields; no web search request count exists.

gaps.impact: Go under-reports and under-prices server-side WebSearch usage relative to TS once provider-native search is available.

gaps.title: Input schema strictness and validation error text/codes differ
gaps.description: TS publishes a strict zod object with query min(2), optional string arrays, and validateInput returns exact messages and numeric errorCode values for missing query and allowed/blocked conflict. Go's schema has no minLength/additionalProperties equivalent, parseInput ignores unknown JSON fields, Execute trims query and returns different user-visible messages without error codes, and it emits progress before conflict validation.

ts_evidence.note: TS inputSchema is z.strictObject with query z.string().min(2) plus optional allowed_domains/blocked_domains arrays.
validateInput returns 'Error: Missing query' with errorCode 1 and the exact conflict message with errorCode 2.

go_evidence.note: Go JSON schema requires query but does not encode minLength or strict additionalProperties behavior.
parseInput round-trips through json.Unmarshal into a struct, which ignores unknown object fields.
Execute trims query and returns 'Error: query is required' or 'Error: allowed_domains and blocked_domains cannot both be set' without TS error codes.
Existing conflict test only asserts IsError, not TS exact message/errorCode parity.

gaps.impact: Manual/tool-injected calls can be accepted or rejected differently, and clients cannot rely on TS-compatible validation diagnostics.

gaps.title: Go tests cover helpers and known gaps more than the production TS-equivalent path
gaps.description: The current Go suite has useful helper tests for local fallback, normalization, citations, cache keys, policy, and fake server providers, but it does not fail on the absence of a production server-tool provider, extraToolSchemas request shape, beta header emission, live stream server_tool_use/web_search_tool_result parsing, web_search_requests usage, exact output object/duration behavior, or default registry enablement. Some alignment comments are stale relative to the current TS code, so the suite can give a stronger parity signal than the production path deserves.

ts_evidence.note: The TS production path under test should be the queryModelWithStreaming call with extraToolSchemas and querySource:'web_search_tool'.
The important runtime behavior is stream parsing through final Output construction.

go_evidence.note: The src harness asserts providerNative semantics, but only through a mock contract fixture.
A current test intentionally expects the local_fallback vs provider_native gap to remain visible.
Provider-native tests use injected providerSearch functions, not production registry/provider wiring.
Server-tool tests cover the adapter function and setter only; they do not verify Anthropic request construction or stream parsing.
The file header says cases must fail and contains stale gap notes even though several are now passing/already implemented.

gaps.impact: Future changes can pass the current WebSearch tests while still missing the TS production behavior that matters most.

candidate_tasks.title: Add provider/types support for Anthropic-defined web_search server-tool protocol
acceptance: provider.Params can carry Anthropic-defined extra tool schemas such as {type:'web_search_20250305', name:'web_search', allowed_domains, blocked_domains, max_uses}.
Anthropic request construction emits the web_search_20250305 server tool and web-search-2025-03-05 beta header where TS does.
Streaming and non-streaming Anthropic responses preserve/convert server_tool_use and web_search_tool_result blocks without dropping unknown server-side data.
types.Usage carries server_tool_use.web_search_requests without breaking existing token/cache usage callers.
No ordinary Go client tool is accidentally serialized as an Anthropic-defined server tool.

candidate_tasks.title: Wire WebSearchTool to the provider-native server tool in production registry/query lifecycle
acceptance: A default WebSearch registered by SetupRegistry uses the provider-native web_search_20250305 path when the active provider/model supports TS WebSearch.
allowed_domains and blocked_domains are passed to the server tool before search rather than only post-filtered after a local search.
Local DDG search is not the default production path; if retained, it is explicitly gated as an unavailable-provider fallback that cannot mask server-tool errors.
WebSearch uses the request context/abort lifecycle rather than a separate fixed local-only timeout when running provider-native search.
The existing local fallback gap test is either removed or inverted to assert provider_native parity.

candidate_tasks.title: Remove or make TS-compatible the local WebSearch cache lifecycle
acceptance: Repeated WebSearch calls do not return synthetic cache://websearch citations.
If any cache remains, cached data preserves the original result list/URLs and is disabled for provider-native server-tool calls unless TS has equivalent behavior.
No results are cached as already formatted model-facing strings.
Tests prove same query/domain filters either triggers fresh provider-native execution or returns byte-for-byte equivalent original source URLs.

candidate_tasks.title: Align WebSearch output, citation formatting, empty result, duration, and server error rendering
acceptance: Go can represent the TS Output shape: query, results array of strings/search result objects, and durationSeconds.
Search result objects preserve tool_use_id and Links JSON contains only title/url unless TS source behavior changes.
Empty results still flow through the TS-style header/reminder path instead of plain 'No results found.' when a WebSearch call completes.
web_search_tool_result error envelopes render as 'Web search error: <error_code>' result strings and are not silently replaced by local fallback results.
Result UI/metadata can derive TS-equivalent search count and duration.

candidate_tasks.title: Align WebSearch progress events with TS streamed server-tool lifecycle
acceptance: No progress event is emitted for inputs that fail validation before TS would call the tool.
query_update is emitted from the actual server_tool_use query stream, including changed query text.
search_results_received includes both resultCount and query with TS-compatible naming and values.
Provider-native success emits search_results_received exactly when web_search_tool_result arrives.
Cache/fallback paths do not emit misleading fake server-tool progress.

candidate_tasks.title: Implement TS-compatible WebSearch enablement and permission suggestion metadata
acceptance: WebSearch is hidden/disabled for providers and models where TS WebSearchTool.isEnabled() returns false.
Blanket deny rules prevent WebSearch from being visible before model tool selection, matching TS getTools filtering.
Permission checks can return a WebSearch passthrough decision with the TS message and a localSettings addRules suggestion for {toolName:'WebSearch'}.
Generic permission behavior for other tools is unchanged.

candidate_tasks.title: Track server_tool_use.web_search_requests through Go usage, cost, and session state
acceptance: Go Usage includes a server-tool-use bucket with web_search_requests.
Anthropic provider stream and non-stream fallback copy web_search request counts from API usage.
Session usage/status/cost surfaces include web search request counts where TS reports them.
Existing token/cache usage behavior and tests remain unchanged.

candidate_tasks.title: Align WebSearch schema strictness and validation diagnostics
acceptance: Go WebSearch schema expresses query min length and rejects unknown fields when the TS strict object would reject them.
Missing query and allowed/blocked conflict return TS-compatible messages and machine-readable error codes or equivalent metadata.
One-character query behavior is covered and matches the TS schema/validation path selected by the runtime.
Progress callbacks are not fired before validation failures.

candidate_tasks.title: Replace WebSearch helper-only parity tests with production-path conformance fixtures
acceptance: Tests assert the real Go production path emits the Anthropic server-tool request shape including beta header, max_uses, and domain filters.
Stream fixtures cover server_tool_use input_json_delta, web_search_tool_result success, web_search_tool_result error envelopes, and usage.server_tool_use.web_search_requests.
The current local_fallback gap test is retired or inverted once provider-native parity lands.
Stale comments in WebSearch alignment tests are updated so failures represent current known gaps, not already-fixed historical ones.
Fixtures compare TS normalized output against Go normalized output for success, error, empty result, allowed_domains, blocked_domains, and validation failures.
